stories.title: Tyler finally broke through.
stories.body: YINZer 4 LIFE finished 9–5 and captured Tyler’s first Dirty D’s championship, exploding for 217.54 points in the final. Vinny landed in second again, giving him a third runner-up finish and another near-miss in a résumé already packed with podiums.

stories.title: The quarterback pool is already disappearing.
stories.body: The league enters 2026 with 33 confirmed keepers, including 13 quarterbacks. With Superflex starters being protected before the room even opens, the remaining elite RB/WR market should get expensive fast—and anyone still shopping for a second quarterback may have to pay the scarcity tax.

season2025.headline: Tyler traded his way to a first title — then detonated in December.
season2025.overview: Vinny controlled the regular season from the opening month, starting 4-0 and reaching 8-2, but 2025 ultimately became Tyler's season. YINZer 4 LIFE combined a strong keeper/draft base with the league's most aggressive trade schedule, then posted 197.40 in the semifinal and an all-time Dirty D's record 217.54 in the championship. Bobby and Nick supplied the best late-season surges; Dan fell from 6-4 to 6-8; James somehow missed the playoffs despite 1,756.22 points and a +141.94 scoring differential; and Jack's 2-12 collapse was amplified by a cluster of injuries to core players.

teams.narrative: Tyler turned a 5-2 start into the first championship of his Dirty D's career, but the title was not a simple draft-and-coast season. YINZer finished 9-5 with 1,781.50 points, made six completed trades — the most in the league in 2025 — and kept reshaping the roster even after Jayden Daniels' season became injury-riddled. The biggest swings included acquiring Bijan Robinson and Brock Purdy and later adding Stefon Diggs and George Pickens. Then the playoff lineup detonated: 197.40 in the semifinal and a league-record 217.54 in the championship game. The 2025 keeper base was Jayden Daniels, Trey McBride and Chuba Hubbard. For 2026, Daniels and McBride return with George Pickens, but $88 is already committed; the next build needs to find running-back value and depth without much room for another massive purchase.

Vinny owned the regular season early: 4-0, 6-1 and 8-2 before finishing 10-4 with a league-best 1,817.36 points. Hurts Donut again showed why Vinny has the best regular-season winning percentage in league history, and the roster stayed active with 84 add/drop moves and three trades. The keeper trio of Jalen Hurts, Jahmyr Gibbs and Ja'Marr Chase gave the team a star floor, and the September deal for Puka Nacua added even more ceiling. The only failure was timing: after 157.40 in the semifinal, the offense ran into Tyler's record-setting final and scored 118.00. In 2026, Gibbs and Chase are still the foundation with Caleb Williams at quarterback; the challenge is turning another elite regular-season roster into the first championship rather than another silver trophy.

Bobby's season was the league's clearest second-half surge. Slim Shiesty sat 3-4 after seven weeks, then went 6-1 to close the regular season at 9-5 with a +222.22 point differential. That recovery happened without a single completed trade, so the comeback was driven by the roster already in place and targeted waiver work. Joe Burrow's September turf-toe injury removed the most expensive keeper for most of the fantasy season, which makes the late run even more impressive. Bobby beat Ben 149.82-140.28 in the quarterfinal, scored 174.58 in a semifinal loss to Tyler, then took third. The core comes back almost unchanged in 2026 — Burrow, Chase Brown and De'Von Achane — leaving $129 to rebuild the receiving room around a proven RB/QB base.

Brent rebounded from the two-win 2024 disaster with an 8-6 season, 1,693.64 points and a fourth-place finish. LongSpurs was never far from the playoff line, and the October swap of Aaron Rodgers for Trevor Lawrence became the season's clearest quarterback reset. The expensive draft bets were Josh Jacobs ($48) and Patrick Mahomes ($30), while the detected keeper group was Justin Jefferson, Nico Collins and Courtland Sutton. Brent then produced one of the best playoff games of the season — 189.06 to eliminate Nick — before dropping to 106.06 in the semifinal. The 2026 roster starts Jefferson, Lawrence and Travis Etienne for only $56 total, which creates a $132 max bid and one of the league's best combinations of flexibility and existing top-end talent.

Nick had to manufacture a playoff berth. Strouds Chicken was 4-6 after Week 10, then won four straight to reach 8-6 while finishing third in regular-season scoring at 1,758.48. The defining move was the November trade with Tyler: Nick sent Bijan Robinson and Daniel Jones for Dak Prescott and Javonte Williams. It solved quarterback depth and helped the stretch run, but it also sent an elite RB into the eventual champion's lineup. The postseason ended immediately when Brent dropped 189.06 in the quarterfinal. The 2025 keeper core was C.J. Stroud, Brock Bowers and Bijan. For 2026, Stroud stays, but the roster pivots to Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Javonte Williams; with $127 left, finding a true RB1 is the obvious draft-day priority.

Ben's 8-6 record was more impressive than the raw scoring rank suggests because Cheese Curds absorbed 1,766.82 points against — one of the harshest schedules in the league. The roster did not rely on trades at all, instead winning seven FAB claims and spending $70 to patch holes around a top-heavy auction led by Kyren Williams, CeeDee Lamb and Ladd McConkey. Ben still made the playoffs and scored 140.28 in the quarterfinal, only to lose a strong game to Bobby's 149.82. CeeDee Lamb was the lone detected 2025 keeper. The 2026 construction is completely different: Kenneth Walker, Jordan Love and Sam Darnold lock in RB plus both quarterback slots for $60, leaving $140 and a clear mandate to buy receiving firepower.

Dan's 2025 season flipped in the wrong direction at exactly the wrong time. Playin with my Ditka reached 6-4 with a positive scoring differential, then lost the final four regular-season games and missed the playoffs at 6-8 despite scoring 53.44 more points than opponents overall. Dan was active in the trade market, turning Xavier Worthy and J.J. McCarthy into Drake London and later moving Bo Nix in a three-player package. Saquon Barkley and Bo Nix were the detected keepers, but the roster never found enough late-season stability around them. The 2026 reset is strategically interesting: Drake Maye and Jaxson Dart solve both quarterback slots for only $32, Cam Skattebo adds a cheap RB, and Dan enters with $161 left and a $149 max bid — ideal conditions to attack premium RB/WR talent.

Jake nearly pulled off one of the better recoveries of the season. Beginners luck opened 1-3, climbed back to 5-5 and finished 8-6, but lost the crowded tiebreak for the final playoff spots. The final scoring line was almost perfectly neutral — 1,629.12 PF and 1,653.16 PA — and the team never completed a trade, instead spending $75 across three successful FAB bids. Jonathan Taylor, George Kittle and Baker Mayfield formed the detected keeper base. The 2026 keepers are Taylor, Mayfield and Rome Odunze for $62, giving Jake a clean RB1/QB1/WR starter framework and $138 to chase a second quarterback plus another premium receiver.

James produced one of the strangest stat lines in the archive: Dirty Mike scored 1,756.22 points with a +141.94 point differential and still finished 6-8. The roster was good enough to score like a playoff team, but the weekly results never aligned. James stayed aggressive with 72 add/drop moves and three trades, including the late acquisition of Bucky Irving just as Irving was returning from his long foot/shoulder absence. The $62 Christian McCaffrey auction buy also paid off spectacularly — McCaffrey played all 17 games and won NFL Comeback Player of the Year. Lamar Jackson and Jameson Williams were the detected 2025 keepers. In 2026, Lamar remains the anchor alongside Rashee Rice and Quinshon Judkins, leaving $140 for a roster that probably needs less reinvention than the 6-8 record implies.

Fritz started 3-1, but Watching Golf slowly slid back to 6-8 and finished almost exactly even in scoring differential (-18.28). The draft itself had plenty of recognizable talent — Drake London, James Cook, Breece Hall and a cheap Amon-Ra St. Brown — yet the roster was unusually quiet afterward: only seven add/drop moves and zero FAB claims. Fritz did make two trades, including moving London for Xavier Worthy and J.J. McCarthy, but there was never a sustained late push. Keon Coleman was the only detected 2025 keeper. That restraint creates the most dramatic 2026 reset in the league: Fritz has no keepers, the full $200 budget, 16 empty roster spots and a $185 max bid. No one has more freedom on draft day.

Jack's season was wrecked by both performance and injuries. Annie's Boobs started 2-2 and then lost ten straight, finishing 2-12 with the league's fewest points (1,329.54) and the most points against (1,811.68). The original roster was built around expensive RB bets Bucky Irving and Alvin Kamara plus Malik Nabers and Brian Thomas Jr.; Nabers tore his ACL in Week 4, Irving missed the middle of the season with foot/shoulder injuries, and Kamara missed the final six NFL games. Jack tried to change course with four trades — including moving Bucky before his return and swapping Brock Purdy for Chuba Hubbard and Marcus Mariota — but the season never stabilized. Nabers and Brian Thomas Jr. were the detected 2025 keepers. For 2026 the team keeps Justin Herbert, Nabers and Zay Flowers for $62, creating a receiver-heavy reset with $138 left; the draft plan has to rebuild running back and secure a second Superflex quarterback.

Jeff spent the first half of 2025 digging out of an impossible hole. El Jefe started 0-7 before improving to 4-10, but 1,392.40 points was still the second-lowest total in the league. The auction was extremely concentrated: Ashton Jeanty cost $62, Josh Allen $45, Tee Higgins $36 and Terry McLaurin $28, leaving very little margin when the supporting pieces did not hit. Jeff made no trades and only seven add/drop moves, so there was limited roster turnover once the season went sideways. Josh Allen was the detected 2025 keeper. The 2026 approach is much cheaper around Allen: Bhayshul Tuten and Jakobi Meyers join him for only $63 total, leaving $137 and a $125 max bid. The biggest opportunity is to use that flexibility earlier rather than waiting for the season to dictate the rebuild.
